meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: by the next regular payday (or the 31-day deadline in 109.03(1), if earlier)
facts.summary: Wisconsin: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due by the next regular payday (or the 31-day deadline in 109.03(1), if earlier).
facts.evidence_quote: Any employee, except a sales agent employed on a commission basis, not having a written contract for a definite period, who quits employment or who is discharged from employment shall be paid in full by no later than the date on which the employee regularly would have been paid under the employer's established payroll schedule or the date of payment required under sub. (1), whichever is earlier.

facts.summary: Wisconsin: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due by the next regular payday (or the 31-day deadline in 109.03(1), if earlier).
facts.evidence_quote: Any employee, except a sales agent employed on a commission basis, not having a written contract for a definite period, who quits employment or who is discharged from employment shall be paid in full by no later than the date on which the employee regularly would have been paid under the employer's established payroll schedule or the date of payment required under sub. (1), whichever is earlier.

facts.summary: Wisconsin basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.

facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)

facts.summary: Wisconsin: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Monthly (note 25).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 25: Wisconsin. Most employers must pay workers all wages earned at least monthly, with no longer than 31 days between pay periods. The only employees exempted from this requirement are employees engaged in logging (must be paid at least quarterly), those engaged in farm labor (must be paid at least quarterly), unclassified employees of the UW system (left to the system), part-time firefighters and part-time emergency medical technicians (must be paid at regular intervals, at least annually), school employees who voluntarily request payment over 12 months, and employees covered under a valid collective bargaining agreement establishing a different frequency for wage payments. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Wisconsin is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).

facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
